_comment: Agents known to be scheduled nowhere as of 2026-07-30, when check_orphan_agents() first ran. Accepted ONLY until the full board triages each one SCHEDULE/RETIRE/DELETE under proposal ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents. This list may only ever SHRINK. Never add an entry to silence a new finding — a new orphan is a hard failure by design.
change_log: 2026-07-30 REMOVED dynamic_position_sizer.py, position_aging_agent.py — they no longer trip the check: neither writes an output that another module reads. (Both are still unscheduled; they are a lesser problem and stay in the ARCH triage.)

2026-07-30 ADDED ml_feature_drift_monitor.py, ml_longterm_label_checker.py — NOT a new regression and NOT a silenced finding. Two bugs in check_orphan_agents() were hiding them on the day this baseline was written: (1) test files were barred from being scheduler ROOTS but could still be pulled into the reachability set and relay from there, so the WIRED_AGENTS list added to test_pipeline_smoke.py made nine baselined orphans look scheduled; (2) the audit read only new_crontab.txt, a Mac-path TEMPLATE that had drifted 10 agents behind the VM's live crontab. Both are fixed; these two were always day-one orphans and belong in the same board triage.

2026-07-31 ADDED risk_limit_governor.py — NOT a new regression and NOT a silenced finding, same situation as the 2026-07-30 addition above. The reachability walk matched a module's name anywhere in another module's TEXT, so a mention inside a docstring or comment counted as a call; that prose reachability was hiding this agent. Fixed by walking code only (_code_only). Verified against ground truth before adding: the live VM crontab has 0 occurrences of risk_limit_governor across 67 job lines, and config.py:99 reads data/risk_limit_overrides.json in real code — a file this agent has never once produced, so config falls back to defaults and the asymmetric risk bands the sign-off ledger work added have never actually applied. Goes to the board with the other 11 under ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents; my read is SCHEDULE.

2026-07-31 REMOVED risk_limit_governor.py, macro_regime_model.py, edgar_transcript_agent.py, institution_performance_tracker.py, ml_improvement_loop.py — SCHEDULE verdict under ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents. All five are now installed in the VM's live crontab (12:40 / 12:50 weekdays, 23:20 daily, Sun 07:40, Sat 06:30 UTC) and appear in data/vm_crontab_snapshot.txt, which is what the check measures against. Each was smoke-run on the VM at exit 0 BEFORE being scheduled — scheduling a producer means owning its output, and an agent that crashes on a cron is a louder failure than one that never runs. 12 known orphans → 7.

2026-08-01 REMOVED apex_system_cit_agent.py, fi_cit_agent.py, ml_longterm_label_checker.py, ml_validate_longterm.py — SCHEDULE, not a detector change. Corroborated against the LIVE VM crontab (crontab -l, 1 job line each) and mirrored into data/vm_crontab_snapshot.txt, per the 2026-07-30 rule that a disappearance from this list must be proven independently of the detector that cleared it.

2026-08-21 ADDED overnight_board_sprint.py — NOT a new regression and NOT a silenced finding. Third instance of the same detector bug as the 2026-07-30 and 2026-07-31 additions above, one layer deeper. The reachability walk counted any mention of a module stem as employment; _code_only() had already stopped prose from counting, but ORDINARY STRING LITERALS were kept on purpose, so a module name sitting in a plain data table still read as a call. wake_agent.py's AGENT_REGISTRY lists ~50 scripts by filename (a wake is on-demand; nothing schedules wake_agent itself), hr_agent.py's _GOVERNANCE_CHAIN is a frozenset naming the officers HR has never reviewed, and strategic_roadmap.py describes agents in prose fields. Being wakeable is not employment, and a list of the unwatched is not proof of watching. Fixed by walking INVOCATIONS via AST (_invocation_edges): imports, plus module names appearing as literal arguments to subprocess/runpy/importlib calls only. Measured effect: modules reachable from a scheduler root fell 183 → 157. Verified against ground truth before adding, per the 2026-07-30 rule: the live VM crontab has 0 occurrences of overnight_board_sprint across 143 non-comment job lines, and signoff_ledger.py:635 independently records the same fact. It writes cit_approved_proposals.json, read by 7 modules including board_meeting.py and deputy_board.py. Goes to the board under ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents; verdict not yet recorded.

2026-08-21 NOTE (not a baseline change) — the detector fix above surfaced exactly one NEW hard finding, and that is itself the finding. check_orphan_agents only reports an unscheduled agent that writes a data/*.json OTHER MODULES READ. That narrowing is deliberate and defended in the code, but it means an agent whose product is not a consumed JSON file is invisible here no matter how central it is. Cross-checked on 2026-08-21 against every scheduler on both hosts (VM crontab, VM systemd timers, Mac crontab, launchd, catch_up.py JOB_REGISTRY, main.py, Claude scheduled tasks): 25 agent modules run NOWHERE, including position_risk_monitor.py (the circuit breaker), deputy_monitor.py (stop-loss enforcement) and cit_watchdog.py. The control that DOES price this correctly is agent_sweep.py's AGENT_UNSCHEDULED — which found 43 on 2026-08-17 and is itself on no schedule. Do not widen this check to compensate; wire agent_sweep instead.

change_log.why: Chairman-approved VM crontab batch 2026-08-28 scheduled the ML research-team chain (queue row AUD-20260702094001). The ratchet is shrink-only, so an agent that gained a scheduler MUST leave the baseline or the next genuine orphan hides behind a stale entry.

NOT a new regression and NOT a silenced finding — fourth instance of the same detector bug class as the 2026-07-30 / 07-31 / 08-21 additions above, now at the loose-fallback layer. scheduler_reachable() still runs an agent_roster.indexed_search word-level fallback on modules with unresolved invocation edges (dynamic subprocess/importlib calls), and apex_system_cit_agent.py — which IS scheduled on the VM — fits that profile. Its _CRON_LOG_CHECKS table held the string literal "fe_cit_agent" as a tuple key, which the loose fallback matched as a word and spuriously treated as an invocation edge from apex_system_cit_agent (scheduled) to fe_cit_agent.py (not scheduled). The 2026-08-21 fix narrowed primary resolution to AST _invocation_edges but KEPT the loose fallback deliberately (over-reaching for the orphan question means fewer false orphan accusations; the error should land where it is cheap). Removing the dead string from _CRON_LOG_CHECKS in commit 33e1f4a — which was itself a cleanup of 8 entries that named scripts no longer scheduled anywhere — severed that loose edge and surfaced the long-standing orphan. Hypothesis proven under the current build: OLD apex_system_cit_agent code → agent_roster.indexed_search('fe_cit_agent', as_word=True) = TRUE; NEW code → FALSE. Verified against ground truth before adding, per the 2026-07-30 rule: live VM crontab (ssh apex-capital 'crontab -l') has 0 occurrences of fe_cit across 484 lines; data/vm_crontab_snapshot.txt independently confirms the same; and fe_cit_agent.py has not appeared in the VM crontab in any of the last 10 snapshot commits (its docstring claims 'Runs daily at 11 AM UTC (cron: 0 11 * * *)' — documented, never built). Writes chairman_action_required.json (40 readers) and fe_approved_picks.json / fe_watchlist.json / fe_rejected_picks.json / fe_pipeline_log.json. Goes to the board under ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents; verdict recorded in triage below; my read is SCHEDULE (direct First Eagle equity analog of fi_cit_agent.py, which went SCHEDULE on 2026-07-31 with cron 30 13 * * 1-5 and has been clean since).

triage._comment: Verdicts for board proposal ARCH-2026-0730-orphan-agents. Recorded 2026-07-31 with per-agent evidence. known_orphans is NOT shrunk here: an entry may only leave that list once the agent is actually in cron, and installing cron is the Chairman's call. Verdict != done.

apex_system_cit_agent.py.evidence: Runs clean on the VM (exit 0, 12 proposals raised). Writes chairman_action_required.json, read by 21 modules. Its own docstring says 'Runs daily at 1 PM UTC (cron: 0 13 * * *)' but the VM crontab has no such entry among 74 jobs — documented, never built. Its GCP-IP check was host-blind until 2026-07-31 (9d293a4); it is now metadata-gated and verified silent off-VM.

fi_cit_agent.py.evidence: Same consumed output contract (chairman queue, 21 readers). Exits 0.

ml_longterm_label_checker.py.evidence: Was blocked on a missing outcome_365d column; that is resolved and it exits 0. Writes ml_longterm_suggestions.json.

ml_validate_longterm.py.evidence: Exits 0. Writes longterm_validation_report.json, read by apex_improvement_board.py and ml_longterm_cit_agent.py.

ml_longterm_experiment_runner.py.evidence: Producer with no executable consumer. Its queue file has NEVER been produced. The upstream improvement agent's 9 suggestions carry no executable lever — this runner can only select a feature set, so bridging them would manufacture 9 results for 9 untested hypotheses. Guarded now by an UNRUNNABLE branch (c284e15). Schedule only after a suggestion format that names a lever this runner can actually pull.

ml_longterm_improvement_agent.py.evidence: Same bridge. Its output has no consumer that can act on it.

ml_feature_drift_monitor.py.blocker: recent window is calendar-based; its input is quarterly
ml_feature_drift_monitor.py.evidence: Verified on the VM: 'Recent window has only 0 rows (min 30). Skipping.' — recent=0, historical=24,576. Root cause is a design mismatch, not an outage: _fetch_windows() defines 'recent' as the last 60 days, but pipeline_snapshots is written on the 13F filing calendar — Feb/May/Aug/Nov, 2-3 distinct dates per quarter, unchanged for four years (last cluster 2026-05-15, next due mid-Aug). So for roughly two months in every three the recent window is empty BY CONSTRUCTION and this monitor can only skip. Scheduling it as-is buys a weekly no-op that reads like a clean run. Fix before scheduling: compare the latest filing cluster to the prior one, not a fixed 60/180-day window.

fe_cit_agent.py.evidence: Direct First Eagle equity analog of fi_cit_agent.py (Fixed Income CIT, SCHEDULE verdict 2026-07-31, cron 30 13 * * 1-5). Writes chairman_action_required.json (same consumed output contract as fi_cit; 40 readers today), plus fe_approved_picks.json (7 readers incl. apex_improvement_board, fe_board, logic_team, fi_risk_monitor), fe_watchlist.json (9 readers), fe_rejected_picks.json, fe_pipeline_log.json (9 readers). Not smoke-run on the VM before this entry — scheduling a producer means owning its output, per the 2026-07-31 note, so verdict is PENDING until Chairman either (a) runs ~/venv/bin/python3 fe_cit_agent.py on apex-capital at exit 0 and installs the proposed_cron (becomes SCHEDULE, remove from known_orphans the same day per the ratchet), or (b) RETIRE/DELETE if the First Eagle pod is already covered elsewhere. The agent's own docstring claims 'Runs daily at 11 AM UTC (cron: 0 11 * * *)' — fix the weekday-only recommendation here if going with SCHEDULE, since the FE pod feeds the weekday pipeline. My read: SCHEDULE, but the Chairman decides and smoke-runs come before cron install.
